analysis.title: Vols Lower, Gold Higher After Blue Sweep / Data-Centre Challenges / AMD Results
key_insights: After Democrats won both houses of Congress in the US midterms, equities reversed an initial knee-jerk sell-off. European equities are +1.1%, US equity futures point to +0.5%, DXY is -0.5%, the US 10y yield is slightly lower at 4.92%, VIX is below 19 and MOVE is below 100. Gold is +2.9% at $4,044/oz.

NBC News has called 54 Senate seats for Democrats vs 44 for Republicans, with the last two leaning Democratic. NBC estimates the House at 258 Democrats vs 177 Republicans. Trump keeps the veto, and Democrats gain influence over appointments, committees and investigations.

UBS Macro Sales lists possible market effects: lower US rates (less geopolitical escalation risk, slower spending growth under gridlock), higher equities (lower oil and rates mean fewer Fed hikes), a stronger dollar (strong US data, weak rest of world per FX Strategy), and some scrutiny on tech from tougher data center construction rules.

Democratic candidates who campaigned on scrutinising data centre development won in Texas, Georgia and Ohio. In Texas, Gina Hinojosa won on a promise of a moratorium on data centre development pending new legal safeguards (FT). An NBC exit poll found 56% said AI and data centres were a crucial or major factor in their vote. UBS says to watch for the AI and hyperscaler complex pricing more regulatory and execution risk.

AMD rose 8.5%, roughly in line with the ~8.6% implied move, after a Q3 beat and a Q4 revenue guide above expectations. Data Center was the standout and Client was slightly light as anticipated. Expectations had been reset lower after INTC's report.

AMD Q3 reported: revenue $13.38bn vs $13.1bn expected, EPS $2.09 vs $1.95, Data Center revenue $8.55bn vs $8.25bn, Client $2.92bn vs $3.08bn, Embedded $1.11bn vs $1.08bn, gross margin 55.9% vs 56%, opex $3.56bn vs $3.66bn estimate, capex $648mn vs $861.3mn, free cash flow $554mn vs $793mn.

AMD guided Q4 revenue to $17bn plus or minus 3% vs $16.3bn expected, with gross margin around 55% vs 55.3% expected. Management cited stronger Instinct and EPYC demand and expects growth to accelerate in Q4 as Helios and Venice production scales.

Eurozone October HICP inflation rose 0.2pp to 4.0% y/y, in line with consensus. Energy inflation rose 1.9pp to 20.8% y/y, driven by Italian electricity tariffs, partly offset by a temporary German fuel tax cut. Food inflation rose 0.3pp to 1.6% (UBS forecast 1.7%). Core was in line with consensus but slightly below UBS's 2.6% forecast. The final estimate is due 18 November.
Bundesbank President Nagel said a December ECB hike is 'very likely necessary' unless the inflation outlook improves significantly. The ECB held rates last week. The Dec. 17 meeting is pricing 22bp.

The ECB wage tracker shows negotiated wage growth of 2.7% in H2 2026 and 2.8% in H1 2027, easing to 2.4% in Q3 2027. Excluding one-offs, it rises from 2.6% in 2026 to an average 2.8% over the first three quarters of 2027.
Bank of Canada raised its policy rate 25bp to 2.5%. Governor Macklem said further increases may be necessary, with inflation projected at or above 3% through much of 2027 and near 2% by mid-2028.

The Riksbank raised rates 25bp to 2% as expected and said further hikes are likely in the coming year, in line with its September forecast. It will fund SEK200bn of FX reserves with foreign currency loans via the national debt office, which it says is not a monetary decision.

Fed Chair Warsh's balance sheet task force is expected to report early next year. UBS expects it to conclude that shrinking the balance sheet requires making reserves less attractive for banks to hold.

UBS Rates Strategy sees Treasury borrowing estimates $12bn above its forecast, or $38bn below after cash-balance adjustments. It expects unchanged coupon auction sizes at Wednesday's refunding, a possible removal of 'at least' from forward guidance, and a first auction size adjustment in May 2027. Unchanged sizes could steepen the 10s/30s curve and cheapen long-end spreads.

New Zealand Q3 employment fell 0.1% q/q and the unemployment rate rose to 5.7%, the highest since 2015. UBS still expects RBNZ to hike 25bp to 3.00% in December and again in February, with a risk the December hike slips to February after Q4 CPI (UBS 4.2%, RBNZ 4.4%).

UBS Australia Economics expects the RBA to hold at 4.85% for a sustained period after three board members voted against a hike and the tightening bias was dropped. Any further hike is more likely in February 2027. Markets price cuts from March, which UBS thinks is too early, with a cutting cycle more likely to start in late 2027.

UBS analyst David Vogt sees downside risk for Apple from a Services slowdown and margin pressure. Services grew about 10% y/y, and the December guide is 8-9% vs UBS at 11.5%. He expects FY27 revenue growth of roughly 10-11% on flat iPhone units and higher ASPs. Margins face pressure as the tariff benefit rolls off, memory costs rise and 3nm capacity stays constrained.

market_movers.rationale: Shares rose 8.5% after a Q3 beat (revenue $13.38bn vs $13.1bn, EPS $2.09 vs $1.95) and a Q4 revenue guide of $17bn vs $16.3bn expected, led by Data Center.
UBS's David Vogt sees Services deceleration (guide of 8-9% for December vs UBS 11.5%) and margin pressure as a risk to the premium multiple.
INTC's report reset expectations for AMD lower ahead of AMD's results.

sector_views.rationale: UBS Macro Sales says tougher data center construction rules could raise costs and slow the buildout, while momentum remains healthy.

earnings_insights: AMD Q3 reported (4 Nov): revenue $13.38bn vs $13.1bn consensus, EPS $2.09 vs $1.95 consensus. The report does not say whether EPS is GAAP or adjusted.
AMD Q3 reported segments: Data Center $8.55bn vs $8.25bn expected, Client $2.92bn vs $3.08bn expected, Embedded $1.11bn vs $1.08bn expected. Gross margin was 55.9% vs 56% expected.
AMD Q4 guidance: revenue $17bn plus or minus 3% vs $16.3bn consensus, gross margin around 55% vs 55.3% consensus.
AMD Q3 reported cash items: capex $648mn vs $861.3mn expected, free cash flow $554mn vs $793mn expected, opex $3.56bn vs $3.66bn estimate.
Apple reported a quarter with better revenue on a strong iPhone print. Services grew about 10% y/y and the December guide is 8-9% vs UBS estimate of 11.5%. Services is now a mid-20% share of revenue.

risk_factors: Democratic scrutiny or a moratorium on data centre construction could slow the AI infrastructure buildout and raise costs.
Treasury leaving coupon auction sizes unchanged could pressure the 10s/30s curve steeper and cheapen long-end spreads.
Apple's Services deceleration and margin pressure (tariff benefit rolling off, higher memory costs, constrained 3nm capacity) could weigh on its premium multiple.
Energy prices and US tariffs add uncertainty for central bank decisions.
RBNZ could delay its December hike to February if Q4 CPI disappoints.
vol_and_positioning: VIX is below 19 vols and MOVE has edged below 100 vols after the midterm result.
AMD's 8.5% move was roughly in line with the ~8.6% implied move.
geopolitical: Democrats won majorities in both houses of Congress in the US midterms, with Trump retaining the veto.
UBS Macro Sales cites reduced risk of geopolitical escalation, which means steady or lower oil prices.
Iran tensions and the Middle East outlook are the subject of a UBS discussion with Suzanne Maloney.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS Macro Sales says momentum in tech remains healthy, equities rebounded after the initial sell-off, and the US economy remains strong.
tension_points.bear_case: Democratic wins in Texas, Georgia and Ohio on platforms of scrutinising data centre construction could raise costs and slow the AI buildout. Texas's Hinojosa promised a moratorium pending new legal safeguards.
tension_points.what_invalidates: UBS says to watch the AI trade and hyperscaler/data centre complex for signs the market starts pricing greater regulatory and execution risk.

tension_points.bull_case: Borrowing estimates were just $12bn above UBS forecasts, or $38bn below after cash-balance adjustments, which supports unchanged coupon auction sizes.
tension_points.bear_case: Keeping auction sizes unchanged could pressure the 10s/30s curve steeper and cheapen long-end spreads, given interest in possible long-end cuts.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A change to forward guidance, such as removing 'at least' or signalling auction size changes this fiscal year, would differ from UBS's unchanged-size call.
